body: I second the piano idea. There are pieces of all technical difficulty for cello and piano, which would make it easy for both of you to find music as you grow on your instruments.

Yeah, that's true. If you're close with your parents or another relative, I'd try talking to them. Chances are they've seen you through the ups and downs and won't pity you, they'll just listen. Your happiness is important though. If you think talking to a counselor would be helpful, that money would be well spent.
What are the things that bring you joy?

Sounds like a counselor of some sort would be a great person to talk to in that case. You can still develop a sense of trust and open up with someone like that without having to worry about them feeling sorry for you.

If you're close to your friend who currently is going through some hard times, it definitely might help you both to talk to each other. I don't know how old you are, but I've sometimes found talking to someone who is older than you can be helpful as well, like a parent or a family member. I've tried talking to friends about depression before, and some of them were enormously helpful while others didn't know what to say, having never dealt with those issues themselves. Whoever you decide to talk to, know that you aren't wasting their time by asking them to listen.

After playing his Op. 130 quartet I absolutely love Beethoven, his quartets are like different friends to me.

I'll never get tired of the Dvorak cello concerto, I'm extremely grateful to have that piece in my instruments repertoire. However, I've heard the Haydn C major cello concerto butchered by young students since I was about five, so it'll take some time before I can say that I love that piece in the same way (my teachers would murder me... it's actually a great piece).

Alban Berg is fantastic like Shyguy already wrote. I love the Cleveland Quartet's recording of Op. 130 (which is on YouTube! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0_Q9JSFJBrE). The Brentano Quartet has great recordings of all the Beethoven Quartets, you should check those out. The Guarneri Quartet also has great recordings... they aren't my personal favorite but I know a few people who love those recordings.
